title: US officials tell House hearing the string of November outages was not a cyberattack
date_note: Date of the House Homeland Security hearing (18 Nov) per The Record; the outages Hankook Ilbo lists run 12 to 17 November.
summary: Hankook Ilbo lists outages from 12 to 17 November at Outlook and Teams, an FAA communications system, United Airlines, JPMorgan Chase, Apple and an NSA network. At an 18 November House hearing, The Record reports, FBI Deputy Director Christopher Raia saw "no indication whatsoever" of malicious cyber activity. On 22 November, Reuters reports, DNI Jay Clayton again said they were not coordinated or state-sponsored, attributed them to technical upgrades and said more interruptions will come.
plain: US security officials say a run of outages at several big services was not a coordinated cyberattack; the intelligence chief blames technology upgrades and says more interruptions will come.
exec: US officials quoted by the sources say the outages were not a coordinated cyberattack; the intelligence chief attributes them to technical upgrades and expects more.
impact: Outages named by the article: Outlook and Teams, FAA communications, United Airlines, JPMorgan Chase, Apple services, an NSA internal network.

sources.name: Reuters (via WSAU): US intelligence chief predicts more tech outages as systems undergo upgrades

validation.note: The Record (18 Nov, hearing coverage), Hankook Ilbo and AZ Free News each report officials saying there is no evidence of a coordinated cyberattack; El Financiero (EFE, 20 Nov) reports Trump calling them independent events. Reuters (22 Nov, via WSAU) reports DNI Clayton on CNN and ABC on 22 November attributing the outages to technical upgrades and expecting more interruptions. Hearing transcript not read.
